2. Problem - Existing rigid chiral structures lack the ability to achieve bidirectionally symmetric fabrication, limiting their applications.
3. Method - The authors propose an angle compensation strategy combined with laser-induced self-assembly of pH-sensitive microstructures to restore chiral symmetry.

5. Takeaway - This research provides a new approach for the rapid and controllable manufacturing of chiral metasurfaces, with implications for optical communication and sensing.

3. Method - The researchers fabricated multi-material sandwich structures using FDM 3D printing and tested their mechanical properties after aging in seawater.
4. Key Result - The results indicated that the number of ABS layers affected the mechanical properties, with one layer showing the lowest water absorption.
5. Takeaway - Additive manufacturing can effectively produce durable multi-material parts suitable for marine environments.
